risks.note: A substantial part of Birlasoft's revenue is derived from particular regions and customers; any adverse geopolitical or macroeconomic event in these areas could significantly impact performance, and lack of differentiation in service offerings combined with dependency on a few large clients poses a significant business risk.

Rapid innovation by hyperscalers, enterprise platform providers and data/analytics companies, combined with evolving Agentic AI capabilities, is increasing client demand for emerging-technology expertise and influencing customers' partner selection; the growth of Global Captive Centers (GCCs) in India and low-cost near-shore alternatives is also diverting client spend away from traditional IT services providers such as Birlasoft.

Birlasoft is pivoting from a people-intensive, staff-augmentation model to an AI-first, platform-enabled managed services model; insufficient internal readiness across skills, AI-infused offerings and evolving commercial constructs could cause revenue volatility, margin pressure from sub-optimal AI leverage, competitive vulnerability, and reputational impact.

Stringent and evolving US immigration and visa regulations (including H-1B and L-1 requirements) may restrict the Company's ability to deploy skilled resources onsite, potentially causing project delivery challenges, increased operational and compliance costs, reduced workforce mobility, and delayed project execution in a key geography.

Cybersecurity threats, vulnerabilities and incidents can disrupt business, impact client service delivery, or result in unauthorized disclosure of sensitive information; non-compliance with data privacy regimes such as GDPR, CCPA and India's DPDPA could result in significant regulatory penalties and reputational loss.

risks.risk: Talent resourcing, retention and upskilling risk
risks.note: The IT services industry depends on the ability to attract, develop and retain skilled professionals aligned with fast-evolving technology and business strategy; rapid shifts in skill demand, particularly in niche, high-demand AI areas, create risk if the Company cannot secure or retain such talent.

Birlasoft faces operational, contractual and financial risks in executing customer projects, including the inability to meet contractual obligations and service level agreements, which could impact reputation, revenue, profitability and potentially lead to legal disputes.

Birlasoft's Climate Risk Assessment has identified physical risks such as extreme heat and water scarcity at certain locations, and transition risks from changing regulations, disclosure requirements and stakeholder expectations, which if not addressed proactively could impact operational continuity, client confidence, sustainability ratings and financial performance.

themes.title: AI-led IT services & ER&D transformation
themes.need: Q1FY27 split the bucket three ways: a soft large-cap core, a re-accelerating mid-cap tier, and an outright business-model change. TCS grew constant currency only +0.4% QoQ / +3.2% YoY despite $9.5bn of TCV (including an ~$800mn net-new SKF mega-deal), and its AI-services book annualising $2.6bn (+13.6% QoQ) saw incremental adds DECELERATE from +$125mn to +$75mn - AI is still project revenue, not annuity. WIPRO is the laggard (+0.9% YoY cc, margin -120bps to 16.0%, Q2 guided -1.5% to +0.5%). Mid-caps are outgrowing: TECHM grew +6.6% YoY cc with every vertical up and an 11th consecutive quarter of margin expansion (14.4%, +330bps); MPHASIS's pipeline is at an all-time high, 2.8x its size at the Mphasis.ai launch and +28% YoY, with AI-led deals now 70% of it (from 12%) and BFS pipeline +100% YoY, and its new Tria platform closed multiple opportunities within seven weeks of launch; FRACTAL lifted net income +92% YoY on INR 912.5cr revenue at NRR 117% with zero churn (though only +9% cc, dragged by TMT -22%); KPITTECH won $349M of new deals with 21% of pipeline now productized AI/SDV solutions. Structurally, HCLTECH is entering the AI-datacenter business with an initial investment of up to INR 3,500cr and a 50MW long-term ambition, and PERSISTENT is buying Nagarro at EUR 1.27bn EV to build a $2.9bn / 46,000-person group - European scale is now bought, not built. The new cost line is visas: TATAELXSI crossed INR 1,000cr of quarterly revenue for the first time (INR 1,021.1cr) yet EBIT fell 330bps QoQ, with 220-230bps of it onsite/subcontractor investment the CFO said cannot be passed to customers.
themes.driver: MPHASIS's guide that 'Q2 is positioned to deliver the best sequential constant currency growth we have delivered in three years' is the most falsifiable claim in the sector; then HCLTECH's AI-datacenter build, the PERSISTENT-Nagarro close, and whether TCS's AI incremental adds re-accelerate off +$75mn.

growth_optionality.title: Growth verticals / optionality
growth_optionality.body: AI-led managed services (Cogito platform); ERP modernization with SAP; expansion in U.S. Manufacturing & BFSI verticals; outcome-based contracts; new global partnerships (San Francisco-based leader); Lifesciences vertical leadership

demand_drivers.title: Demand & outlook drivers
demand_drivers.body:
- Performance reflects a subdued demand environment with lower discretionary client spends and a push for productivity benefits by customers, aggravated by recent geopolitical developments
- Technology services sector at an inflection point: AI has moved beyond experimentation to enterprise-wide adoption; near-term demand patterns remain uneven but structural growth drivers remain intact
- Manufacturing is the largest vertical (37.9% of consolidated revenue), followed by BFSI (24.4%), Life Sciences & Services (20.4%), and Energy & Utilities (17.3%)
- Americas continued to be the largest market (86% of consolidated revenue), while Europe emerged as a key growth driver across other geographies
- NASSCOM expects Indian technology spending patterns to remain range-bound in the near term, though AI allocations are likely to rise, constrained by data maturity gaps but supported by large-scale enterprise transformations
- Enterprise AI shifting from experimentation to industrial-scale, outcome-based deployment is expected to create higher-margin, annuity-style engagement opportunities for Indian IT providers
- Growth of the Global Capability Centres (GCC) ecosystem in India (2,000+ units) is affecting the flow of business to traditional IT services providers
- Geopolitical fragmentation — talent mobility restrictions via visa policy, export controls on critical inputs, and regulatory barriers such as the EU's DMA, DSA and AI Act — is raising delivery costs and fragmenting global trade for Indian IT firms
- Talent mobility risk, high attrition in specialised ER&D and AI roles, and wage inflation are squeezing industry margins amid modest net hiring
- Pipeline remains strong, with the Company converting this momentum into consistent, profitable growth
- During the year, Birlasoft secured several strategic, multi-year engagements across Manufacturing, Industrial, Energy and Communications sectors, many anchored in AI-led transformation spanning supply chain optimisation, hyper-automation, agent-driven ERP modernisation and resilience initiatives

other.title: Notable from the deck
other.body:
- [Reinvestment intent] The CEO states the company will "continue to invest in our tech capabilities as well as in our sales force that should further strengthen our deals pipeline over the course of the year"; no capex amount, project or timeline is attached.
- [Macro] Management frames the quarter's 2.3% QoQ revenue growth as "stable performance in the face of a macro-environment that remains challenging".
- [Currency] Reported figures are sensitive to a moving rupee: average $/Rs rate of Rs 85.3 for Q1 FY26, Rs 92.8 for Q4 FY26 and Rs 95.0 for Q1 FY27 (period-end 85.76 / 94.83 / 94.66), which is why dollar revenue fell 0.1% QoQ while rupee revenue rose 2.3%; constant currency revenue is stated as up 0.3% QoQ and down 3.0% YoY.
- [Group] Part of the CKA Birla Group, an Indian multinational with over 35,000 employees and more than 50 manufacturing facilities, whose companies include Birlasoft, GMMCO, National Engineering Industries (NBC Bearings), BirlaNu (formerly HIL), Orient Electric, CK Birla Healthcare, Orient Paper, AVTEC and Neosym.
